page: Amazon Web Services g6f.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. System memory comprises 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU to memory capacity ratio. For hardware acceleration, the instance includes a fractional 0.125 NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture with 3 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local high-speed storage is bundled via a 100 GB NVMe SSD, accompanied by a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results illustrate strong single-core compute performance alongside predictable constraints on parallel throughput. In stress-ng testing, single-core execution placed in the top 25 percent, while multi-core compute settled in the bottom 25 percent due to the two physical core ceiling. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both cached and uncached block sizes placed the instance in the bottom quartile. The fractional NVIDIA L4 accelerator delivers capable prompt-processing throughput for smaller AI models, reaching 1067.94 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model and 69.2 tokens per second on a 7B model. However, autoregressive text generation fell into the bottom decile across evaluated models, reflecting the memory bandwidth and compute boundaries of the fractional slice.

The fractional GPU configuration offers an entry-level pathway to modern Ada Lovelace acceleration without the resource overhead of a full dedicated accelerator. Combined with bundled local NVMe storage and dedicated CPU threads, the instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for lightweight graphics rendering, small-scale computer vision inference, edge model validation, and localized services requiring GPU offload. It is less suited to high-throughput data processing pipelines, dense database indexing, or large language model generative execution.
description: Amazon Web Services g6f.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.4 GHz. Featuring 4 vCPUs across 2 physical x86_64 cores, 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 100 GB NVMe SSD, the platform includes a fractional 0.125 NVIDIA L4 GPU with 3 GB of VRAM. It operates on a 2 Gbps baseline network connection. Benchmark assessments demonstrate strong single-core CPU execution alongside bottom-quartile multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics. Inference benchmarks indicate capable prompt ingestion for lightweight models, balanced against modest token generation speeds due to the fractional GPU profile. The configuration delivers a cost-efficient entry point for light graphics processing, small computer vision workloads, and localized model testing requiring hardware acceleration alongside dedicated local NVMe storage.
